mechanisms.definition: Missingness probability is completely independent of both observed and unobserved values.
mechanisms.dataset_example: A student accidentally missed submitting optional certification certificates or workshop attendance log due to technical web portal timeout.
mechanisms.recommended_treatment: Listwise deletion or mean/median imputation without introducing bias.

mechanisms.definition: Missingness depends systematically on observed data, but not on the missing value itself.
mechanisms.dataset_example: Freshmen or second-year students from Tier 3 colleges are less likely to report Mock Interview scores because mock drives were scheduled only for final-year candidates.
mechanisms.recommended_treatment: Conditional / Multiple Imputation (KNN or MICE) conditioned on CollegeTier and Stream.

mechanisms.definition: Missingness depends directly on the unobserved value itself.
mechanisms.dataset_example: Students who scored very poorly on coding assessments chose not to report or save their coding score.
mechanisms.recommended_treatment: Explicit missingness indicator flag (Binary Dummy variable) + median imputation to preserve the informative negative signal.

model_guidance.reason: Features on larger scales dominate gradient updates and bias regularisation penalties.
Euclidean distance calculations are completely distorted by unscaled feature magnitudes.
Variance-maximization projects onto whatever axis has arbitrarily larger units.
Greedy split criteria evaluate individual features independently via rank-order thresholds.

treatment_comparison.description: Preserve all records without deleting duplicate score combinations.
treatment_comparison.risk_assessment: Zero risk of data loss. Preserves legitimate student cohorts with standardized test percentiles.

treatment_comparison.description: Drop records where every feature across all columns is strictly identical.
treatment_comparison.risk_assessment: Safe. True identical rows are pipeline logging repetitions or database insertion duplicates.

treatment_comparison.description: Drop records sharing identical [CGPA, AttendancePercent, CodingTestScore, ...].
treatment_comparison.risk_assessment: High Risk. In a cohort of 50,000 university students, distinct candidates frequently earn identical rounded CGPAs and standardized aptitude percentiles. Removing them distorts branch placement rates.

risks.factor: Coincidental Score Parity in Large Cohorts
risks.explanation: In large engineering institutions (50,000 students), integer score scales (e.g. 75/100 aptitude, 80/100 coding, 7.5 CGPA) naturally lead to multiple students holding the same numerical scores.
Categorical fields like Stream (CS, IT) and CollegeTier (Tier 1, Tier 2) have low cardinalities. High score overlap within these buckets is expected and valid.
Deleting subset duplicates would artificially bias placement percentage estimations and training distributions, producing unfair predictions for common score profiles.

duplicates.verdict: Exact row duplicates: 0 (0.0%). Academic metric duplicates represent valid independent students across the 50k cohort.

educational_theory.mechanism: Analytically minimizes sum of squared residuals without learning rate tuning.
educational_theory.pros: Exact global minimum in one step; no iterations required.
educational_theory.cons: Matrix inversion complexity is O(p^3); ill-conditioned when collinearity exists.

educational_theory.mechanism: Penalizes Euclidean norm of weights; shrinks coefficients toward zero without nullifying them.
educational_theory.pros: Handles multicollinearity and prevents weight explosion.
educational_theory.cons: Does not perform feature selection (all features retain non-zero weights).

educational_theory.mechanism: Penalizes absolute weight magnitudes; drives non-informative feature weights strictly to zero.
educational_theory.pros: Automatic feature selection resulting in sparse, interpretable models.
educational_theory.cons: Arbitrarily selects one feature among correlated predictors and drops the rest.

educational_theory.mechanism: Convex combination of L1 sparsity and L2 grouping properties.
educational_theory.pros: Retains groups of correlated relevant predictors while achieving sparsity.
educational_theory.cons: Requires tuning two hyperparameters (alpha and l1_ratio).

lifecycle_stages.name: Data Ingestion & Dataset Sourcing
lifecycle_stages.description: Ingestion of 50,000 multi-semester student academic, test score, and placement records.

lifecycle_stages.name: Data Quality Profiling & Schema Audit
lifecycle_stages.description: Comprehensive audit of MCAR/MAR/MNAR missingness, exact full-row duplicates, and key subset conflicts.

lifecycle_stages.name: Data Cleaning & Outlier Treatment
lifecycle_stages.description: IQR calculation, Tukey fences, boxplot diagnostics, and empirical comparison of Removal vs Retain vs Winsorization.

lifecycle_stages.name: Feature Engineering & Scaling
lifecycle_stages.description: Derives TechnicalComposite, CGPA tiers, and benchmarks StandardScaler, MinMaxScaler, and RobustScaler without leakage.

lifecycle_stages.name: Leakage-Safe Partitioning (70/15/15)
lifecycle_stages.description: Strict 3-way partition: Train (fitting), Validation (hyperparameters & calibration), Held-out Test (final benchmark).

lifecycle_stages.name: Model Training & Regularization
lifecycle_stages.description: Fits Linear GD, Normal Equation OLS, Polynomial, Ridge (L2), Lasso (L1), Elastic Net, Logistic, Random Forest, AdaBoost.

lifecycle_stages.name: Hyperparameter Optimization & Validation
lifecycle_stages.description: 5-Fold Stratified Cross-Validation, Nested CV (Inner 3-Fold / Outer 3-Fold), and learning/validation curves.

lifecycle_stages.name: Unbiased Held-Out Test Evaluation
lifecycle_stages.description: Single-pass evaluation on held-out test records reporting MAE, MSE, RMSE, R2, ROC-AUC, PR-AUC, and F1 score.

lifecycle_stages.name: Model Packaging & Artifact Registry
lifecycle_stages.description: Encapsulates model binary, feature schema, preprocessor state, library versions, and cryptographic SHA256 checksums.

lifecycle_stages.name: Validated Prediction Serving
lifecycle_stages.description: High-throughput inference endpoints with runtime schema validation, type coercion, and bounded response times.

lifecycle_stages.name: Production Telemetry & Drift Monitoring
lifecycle_stages.description: Tracks inference latency, request volume, Kolmogorov-Smirnov distribution shifts, and Population Stability Index (PSI).

lifecycle_stages.name: Retraining Triggers & Promotion Gate
lifecycle_stages.description: Enforces automated pipeline re-run when drift PSI >= 0.20 or error degradation exceeds 5.0%.

supervised.title: Supervised Learning
supervised.definition: Learning a functional mapping f(X) -> y from labeled historical student records.
supervised.placement_example: Predicting whether a student gets placed (PlacementStatus: 0 or 1) and expected Salary Package (in LPA) given CGPA, CodingTestScore, and Internships.
supervised.key_challenges: Class imbalance, label noise, covariate shift between batches, and feature multicollinearity.

unsupervised.title: Unsupervised Learning
unsupervised.definition: Discovering latent structure, student archetypes, and density clusters in feature space X without target labels.
unsupervised.placement_example: Clustering students into skill archetypes (e.g., Tech Stars, Balanced Achievers, Upskilling Needed) using K-Means and DBSCAN.
unsupervised.key_challenges: Cluster validity evaluation, sensitivity to feature scaling, and absence of an objective ground truth.

reinforcement.title: Reinforcement Learning
reinforcement.definition: Training an agent to maximize cumulative rewards through trial-and-error environment interaction.
reinforcement.placement_example: Curriculum optimization & adaptive course recommendation: An agent suggests mock tests or workshops to maximize placement probability with minimal student workload.
reinforcement.key_challenges: Delayed feedback, exploration vs exploitation tradeoff, and sample inefficiency in educational settings.

training_serving_skew.concept: Training-Serving Skew is the performance discrepancy between training evaluation and production inference.
root_causes: Target Leakage: Including post-placement variables (such as final offer letter status or company allocation) during training.
Inconsistent Pipelines: Preprocessing features with different imputation/scaling parameters offline vs in Flask production endpoints.
Covariate Shift: Changes in input distributions P(X) between historical academic years and incoming graduating batches.
Time Lag & Schema Drift: Missing values or shifted test score grading rubrics not caught before inference.
training_serving_skew.placement_mitigation: Encapsulating preprocessing and scaling within Scikit-Learn Pipelines fitted solely on training splits, with unified schema validation at both training and inference time.

feature_store_architecture.concept: A centralized repository coordinating student feature definitions, storage, and retrieval across training and serving.

dual_storage.offline_store: High-throughput data warehouse / CSV store optimized for historical batch training and semester-by-semester backfills.
dual_storage.online_store: Ultra-low-latency key-value cache (e.g., Redis) retrieving student profile features in under 10ms during live portal prediction queries.

feature_store_architecture.point_in_time_correctness: Ensures historical student features retrieved for training reflect exactly what was known before campus placement drives commenced.
